titleEn: Plant a Row Together, Make a Friend!

pages.text: "I'll stay here." Children from the lower village climbed up the terraced paddies. Today was rice-planting day, when everyone planted together. Dingding slipped behind Grandma's loose trousers.
Grandma put a young rice plant in Dingding's hand. "Try planting a row, too." Dingding held it tightly, but their feet would not move. "I want to plant, too, but..."
In the paddy, the children splashed into rows. Laughter rose to the higher fields. Dingding kept fiddling with the rice plant, still standing on the bank.
Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, held Dingding's hand and entered the paddy with them. Their bare feet sank into the mud. She stood close beside Dingding. "Let's plant just one beside me."
A young water buffalo stood in the next row. "I'm Mungi. I'm from the lower village. What's your name?" Dingding said softly, "...Dingding."
Side by side, they each planted one young rice plant. Two plants stood together above the water. Grandma smiled. "Plant a Row Together, Make a Friend!"
Dingding and Mungi planted one, then another. Soon a straight row reached the far edge. For the first time, Dingding spoke loudly. "Plant a Row Together, Make a Friend!"
At the work-break meal, Dingding and Mungi sat side by side on the bank. Dingding sniffed. Mungi's basket smelled of rice cakes. Faces that had seemed strange that morning now felt friendly.

Dingding knew the steps to making friends. "One, say my name first! Two, stand beside someone in a row! Three, plant together, one plant at a time!" Dingding offered a rice plant to a child standing alone at the row's end. "I'm Dingding. Want to join our row?"

Grandma hugged muddy Dingding, apron and all. Even unfamiliar faces soon became friends when they stood side by side in a row. Dingding held Mungi's hand and swung it. "Plant a Row Together, Make a Friend!"
